positions.pos: Art and design rounds now start themselves. Each strand with a contract (council/loops/<strand>.json, docs/loops.md) names its next round, how it is checked and its budget; when a round ends, the coordinator starts the next one without waiting for you. Your look becomes the veto: work runs at most two rounds past your last look, then waits. A redirect from you rewrites the next round before it starts, and a stop holds every queued round. The spirit art loop is the pilot. Round 3 (eyes, fire crust, water ribbons) is running from your round 2 look; round 4 (the armadillo and pangolin bases in all stages and elements) starts itself when round 3 ends; round 5 (one nation style) waits for your look at round 3. Each of your looks is also saved with its render in council/loops/labels/, for a grader that can later predict your easy calls. This stands unless you flip it.
positions.why: Your words on the loop engineering thread, 2026-10-14: "I do a lot of prompting for the next move instead of that next move being already acted upon", then "Yes I agree with this. What would we need to do to implement". Two rounds ahead keeps a wrong turn to two small rounds.

positions.pos: A round starts itself only when its gate is auto: no money spent, no account signed into or changed, nothing published outside the project, and no council/faces.yaml change. A round that needs your eyes, money or accounts waits and shows up as a step for you instead. Renders, builds on a branch, pull requests and art proof pages count as auto. This stands unless you flip it.
positions.why: Built with loop-ahead-two. Spending and accounts are steps no one can undo by the time you read about them, so they keep needing your word; council/faces.yaml changes only by your ruling (CLAUDE.md).
